title: Don't love me, I belong to my country
takeaway: Sometimes duty to your people comes before your own heart.
scene: This poem turns the love poems around. Someone beautiful is interested in the poet. He tells them, kindly but firmly: I can't. My life belongs to my country and its people, and there's work to do.

original: مینوں پیار کریں نہ شوخ نظر ایہہ دنیا میرے پیار دی نئیں
میں جس باگے وچ وسداہاں رت آوندی ایتھے بہار دی نئیں
transliteration: Mainu pyaar kareen na shokh nazar, eh duniya mere pyaar di nahin
Main jis baage vich vasda haan, rut aaundi ethe bahaar di nahin
translation: Don't love me, playful eyes; this world isn't one for my love.
Spring never comes to the garden where I live.
couplets.story: He tells the person with the flirty eyes: please don't fall for me. The world he lives in has no room for romance. Spring never comes to his garden.

original: ایہہ دل زلفاں دا عاشق نئیں رنگ روپ نگر دا واسی نئیں
میں قوم وطن دا خادم ہاں مینوں لوڑ کسے دلدار دی نئیں
transliteration: Eh dil zulfaan da aashiq nahin, rang roop nagar da vaasi nahin
Main qaum vatan da khaadim haan, mainu lorr kise dildaar di nahin
translation: This heart isn't in love with tresses; it doesn't live in the city of looks.
I'm a servant of my nation and homeland; I don't need a sweetheart.
couplets.story: His heart isn't interested in beautiful hair or pretty faces. He has given himself to serving his country and his people. He doesn't need a girlfriend.

original: میری ایہہ جوانی انج جاپے جویں چانی رات سیالاں دی
مزدور ہاں میں زور اور نئیں مینوں سدھ بدھ حسن خمار دی نئیں
transliteration: Meri eh jawaani inj jaape jiven chaanni raat Siyaalaan di
Mazdoor haan main, zoravar nahin, mainu sudh budh husn khumaar di nahin
translation: My youth may seem like a moonlit night among the Sials,
but I'm a labourer, not a powerful man; I have no head for beauty's intoxication.
couplets.story: Yes, he's young, and his youth might look romantic, like a moonlit night in an old love story. But he's a working man, not a rich or powerful one. He has no time to get drunk on beauty.

original: تیری الہڑ شوخ جوانی تے دل کیہڑا جو نہ ڈلھ جاوے
میری راہ وکھری میرا فرض اچا گل ہور کوئی انکار دی نئیں
transliteration: Teri alhar shokh jawaani te dil kehra jo na dulh jaave
Meri raah vakhri, mera farz uchcha, gall hor koi inkaar di nahin
translation: Whose heart wouldn't melt for your carefree, playful youth?
But my path is different, my duty is higher; there's no other reason for my 'no'.
couplets.story: He admits it. Anyone would fall for someone as young and lively as them. But his path is different, and his duty matters more. That's the only reason he's saying no.

original: میرا تن من مال قربان سدا اس دیش دی آنکھ تے آن اتے
میں جس منزل ول جا رہیا واں اوہ راہ کوئی فرار دی نئیں
transliteration: Mera tan man maal qurbaan sada is desh di aan te shaan utte
Main jis manzil val ja rehiya vaan, oh raah koi faraar di nahin
translation: My body, my mind and my wealth are always ready to be sacrificed for this country's honour.
The destination I'm heading for isn't a road you can run away on.
couplets.story: Everything he has, his body, mind and money, he's ready to give for his country's honour. The road he's on isn't one you can quit halfway.

original: تیرے نیناں دے وچ پیار دسے تیرے انگ انگ اندر شوخی اے
میری جان نثار ہے قوم اتوں مینوں فرصت قول قرار دی نئیں
transliteration: Tere nainaan de vich pyaar dasse, tere ang ang andar shokhi ae
Meri jaan nisaar hai qaum utton, mainu fursat qaul qaraar di nahin
translation: Love shows in your eyes, and playfulness fills every part of you,
but my life is pledged to my nation; I have no time for vows of love.
couplets.story: He can see love in their eyes and liveliness in everything about them. But his life is already promised to his people. He has no time for romantic promises.

original: ایہہ ستی قوم جگانی ایں، ایتھوں رشوت بدی مکانی ایں
اجے لک مہنگائی ہے توڑ رہی، وتھے غربت گھڑی گزار دی نئیں
transliteration: Eh sutti qaum jagaani ain, ethon rishvat badi mukaani ain
Ajje lakk mehngaai hai tor rahi, vatthe gurbat ghari guzaar di nahin
translation: This sleeping nation has to be woken up; bribery and evil have to be wiped out here.
Rising prices are still breaking people's backs, and poverty won't let anyone breathe.
couplets.story: He explains why. His people are 'asleep' and need waking up. Bribery and corruption have to be stopped. Prices keep going up and are crushing families, and the poor can barely get through each day.

original: ایہہ حسن جوانی نئیں رہنی میری گل مٹیارے یاد رکھیں
جے جان وطن تے وار دیویں، فیر کوئی وی بازی ہار دی نئیں
transliteration: Eh husn jawaani nahin rehni, meri gall mutiyaare yaad rakheen
Je jaan vatan te vaar deveen, pher koi vi baazi haar di nahin
translation: This beauty and youth won't last; remember what I say, young woman.
If you give your life for your homeland, then no game is ever lost.
couplets.story: He gives the young woman some advice. Beauty and youth fade. But if you give your life to your country, you can never really lose.

original: تیرا حسن جوانی اک پاسے، میرے شعر شرارے اک پاسے
اٹھ قومی گیت سنا احمدؔ ہور لوڑ کسے گفتار دی نئیں
transliteration: Tera husn jawaani ik paase, mere shair sharaare ik paase
Uth qaumi geet suna Ahmad, hor lorr kise guftaar di nahin
translation: Put your beauty and youth on one side, and my fiery verses on the other.
Get up, Ahmad, sing a song for the nation; no other talk is needed.
couplets.story: He weighs her beauty against his fiery poems, and his poems win. He tells himself: get up, Ahmad, and sing a song for your country. Nothing else needs saying.

why: This is where the book shifts from love poems to poems about Pakistan and society. It shows the poet cared as much about his country as about matters of the heart: corruption, rising prices and poverty.
prompt: Is there a cause you care about enough to put before your own wants?
notes: Marked 'spiritual: none'. The duty here is to the nation, though serving people can itself be a form of worship in Islam. To revisit in the deep pass.
Couplet 5: 'aan' is printed 'آنکھ'; it is read as 'aan te shaan' (honour).
